hypotheses: Hallmark interferon-alpha response is upregulated in CD14 monocytes from COVID-19 patients compared to healthy donors
CD16 monocyte proportion is increased in COVID-19 patients relative to healthy donors
CD8 effector T cells upregulate exhaustion markers in COVID-19 patients versus healthy donors
B cell immunoglobulin gene programs are enhanced in COVID-19 patients compared to healthy donors
Neutrophil inflammatory gene programs are activated in COVID-19 patients relative to healthy donors

claims.claim: Hallmark interferon-alpha response is upregulated in CD14 monocytes from COVID-19 patients compared to healthy donors (mean difference = 0.19, Cohen's d = 1.72)
CD16 monocyte proportion is significantly lower (mean 0.037 vs 0.286, Cohen's d = −2.02) in COVID-19 patients vs healthy donors, opposite to the hypothesis of increase.
CD8eff T cell exhaustion score is higher in COVID-19 patients than healthy donors (mean difference = 0.097, Cohen’s d = 1.14; Welch’s t‑test p = 0.082, based on 6 COVID‑19 and 5 healthy donors).
B-cell activation scores do not differ between COVID-19 and healthy donors (mean difference −0.0029, Cohen's d −0.0737), refuting the hypothesis of enhancement in COVID-19.

Neutrophil degranulation gene‑program donor‑level scores are decreased in COVID‑19 patients compared to healthy donors (mean difference −0.044, Cohen’s d = −1.13), but the difference is not statistically significant (Welch’s p = 0.166).

Hallmark Interferon Alpha Response is upregulated in CD14 monocytes from COVID-19 patients compared to healthy donors, with a large effect size (Cohen's d = 1.721) and statistically significant adjusted p-value (FDR = 0.014334).
CD16 monocyte proportion is lower in COVID-19 patients than in healthy donors (mean difference = -0.2411, Cohen's d = -1.77).
COVID-19 patients have a higher B-cell immunoglobulin gene program donor-level score than healthy donors (mean difference = 0.0675, Cohen's d = 0.98), 7 COVID-19 vs 6 healthy donors.

Neutrophil degranulation gene program scores in neutrophils are lower in COVID-19 patients than healthy donors (mean difference −0.04441, Cohen's d = −1.135, 4 vs 3 donors), opposite to hypothesis of inflammatory gene program activation.
COVID-19 patients show a consistent interferon-stimulated gene program across all major leukocyte cell types
B cells are enriched (cohens_d=1.29) and pDC are depleted (cohens_d=-2.20, p_adj=0.006) in COVID-19 vs normal donors
CD14 Monocyte proportion is increased (cohens_d=0.79) and CD8 T cell proportion is decreased (cohens_d=-1.03) in COVID-19
Top ISG genes upregulated across cell types include STAT1, IFI44, IFI44L, PARP9, and S100A8
